title: Option Pricing on Automated Market Maker Tokens

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper derives the stochastic price process for automated market maker (AMM) tokens from first principles, demonstrating that token prices follow a constant elasticity of variance (CEV) model when net staking flows follow a Brownian diffusion. Closed-form European option prices and liquidity-adjusted Greeks are obtained via the non-central chi-squared distribution. The empirical methodology includes a Monte Carlo validation, a cross-sectional delta-hedged backtest across Bittensor subnets to evaluate ATM hedging errors, and a variance elasticity regression test controlling for pool depth and flow volatility.
extraction.universe: 98 Bittensor subnets with sufficient on-chain history (and subsets of 90 and 82 subnets for specific empirical tests)

key_findings: When net flows into a constant-weighted-product AMM follow a diffusion process, the token price follows a constant elasticity of variance (CEV) process with exponent equal to the numeraire weight (beta = w).
The CEV structure generates a leverage effect where volatility rises as price falls, creating a negative implied volatility skew controlled entirely by pool weights rather than pool depth.

Empirically, realized return variance across Bittensor subnets exhibits a strongly negative price elasticity (median slope -0.86), decisively rejecting geometric Brownian motion and supporting the CEV prediction.

A delta-hedged backtest across Bittensor subnets confirms near-identical hedging errors at the money between CEV and Black-Scholes, consistent with pricing differences being concentrated in the wings.
limitations: The diffusion assumption for staking flows is an approximation, as Shapiro-Wilk tests reject normality and heavy tails indicate occasional large staking events.
Delta-hedging is imperfect due to AMM price impact slippage, though the replication premium is shown to be negligible for deep pools.
Flow volatility is treated as constant while in practice staking activity exhibits time-of-day effects, momentum, and regime changes.
Token prices can be vulnerable to manipulation near option expiry in shallow pools.
